methodologyNotes: Specs sourced from manufacturer pages (Roku, Apple, Nvidia), Wikipedia hardware articles (Amazon Fire TV, Chromecast, Nvidia Shield TV, Roku), and reputable tech reviews (Android Police, 9to5Google). Primary sources were accessed via WebFetch; where a source redirected or blocked, Wikipedia was used as fallback (noted in provenance). US prices are MSRP / launch prices in USD for the base configuration noted in priceNote; prices for Roku Ultra, Roku Streaming Stick 4K, and Roku Express 4K+ were not surfaced from Roku's own product pages (JavaScript-rendered content) and are stated from widely-reported launch prices corroborated by Wikipedia spec tables. Fire TV prices are Amazon announced launch prices as reported by Wikipedia and broad industry coverage. Apple TV 4K price confirmed from Apple's own Shop page. Nvidia Shield TV Pro price confirmed from nvidia.com shield product page. Google TV Streamer price confirmed from 9to5Google review ($99). Onn 4K Pro price ($49.99) and WiFi 6 confirmed from PCWorld and Android Central reviews (re-verified 2026-06-15; prior WiFi 5 and 2024-01 release values were corrected). accessedAt is 2026-06-15 for all sources. Specs: max_resolution is the highest output resolution supported. hdr_formats is a comma-separated string of all confirmed supported HDR formats. wifi is the WiFi generation label (WiFi 5 = 802.11ac; WiFi 6 = 802.11ax dual-band; WiFi 6E = 802.11ax tri-band). storage_gb is internal flash storage in GB for base config. remote_voice is true if a voice-capable remote is included in the box. ethernet is true if an RJ-45 port is built-in on the device itself (not via USB adapter). release is YYYY-MM of US commercial availability.

products.name: Roku Ultra (2024)
products.priceNote: US MSRP, model 4850R; includes Roku Voice Remote Pro (2nd ed.) and HDMI cable
products.provenance: Roku product page (roku.com) confirmed: 4K/60fps, Dolby Vision/HDR10+/HDR10/HLG, WiFi 6 (802.11ax dual-band MIMO), 10/100 Ethernet, Roku Voice Remote Pro, model 4850R. Wikipedia Roku article confirmed processor Realtek 1619BRV, 4 GB storage, 2 GB RAM, released September 2024. MSRP $99.99 is the widely-reported launch price for the 2024 Ultra; Roku's own page was JavaScript-rendered and did not surface price text.

products.name: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K (2nd Gen)
products.provenance: Wikipedia Amazon Fire TV Stick article: 2nd gen released October 18 2023, MediaTek CPU 2.0 GHz, 2 GB RAM, 8 GB storage, 4K, HDR10+/Dolby Vision, WiFi 6 (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax dual-band). Wikipedia Amazon Fire TV article corroborates MediaTek processor and WiFi 6. HLG and HDR10 are standard components of the Fire TV HDR pipeline confirmed in Amazon product documentation; launch price $49.99 is the widely reported figure. Ethernet requires a separate USB-C to RJ-45 adapter (not included).

products.name: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Gen)
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP, model B0CHP9M564; Ethernet requires separate Micro-USB adapter (not included)
products.provenance: Wikipedia Amazon Fire TV Stick article: 2nd gen Max released October 18 2023, MediaTek 2.0 GHz CPU, 2 GB LPDDR4 RAM, 16 GB storage, 4K, Dolby Vision, WiFi 6E (tri-band 802.11ax). Wikipedia Amazon Fire TV article corroborates WiFi 6E and 16 GB. HLG and HDR10/HDR10+ are standard in the Fire TV HDR stack. CORRECTION 2026-06-15: prior priceNote/provenance claimed a USB-C to Ethernet adapter is bundled — this is WRONG. The 4K Max ships with no Ethernet adapter; a wired connection requires a separately purchased Micro-USB (not USB-C) Ethernet adapter. Launch price $59.99 is the widely reported figure. Ethernet column is false because there is no built-in RJ-45 port and no bundled adapter.

products.name: Amazon Fire TV Cube (3rd Gen)
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP; built-in 10/100 Ethernet port on device
products.provenance: VERIFIED 2026-06-15: Amazon developer device-spec page confirmed for Fire TV Cube 3rd gen (released October 25 2022): Amlogic POP1-G octa-core (4x 2.2 + 4x 2.0 GHz), 2 GB LPDDR4 RAM, 16 GB storage, 4K, HDR10/HDR10+/HLG/Dolby Vision, WiFi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax tri-band 2x2 MIMO (= WiFi 6E), and a built-in 10/100 Ethernet (RJ-45) port on the device. CORRECTION: ethernet was previously false with a claim that an adapter was bundled — the 3rd-gen Cube has a built-in RJ-45 Ethernet jack (a key generational upgrade that eliminated the adapter required on prior Cubes); corrected to ethernet=true. CORRECTION: HLG was omitted but Amazon's own spec lists HDR10/HDR10+/HLG/Dolby Vision; added. Alexa Voice Remote included; hands-free Alexa. Launch price $139.99 is the widely-reported figure.

products.name: Google TV Streamer 4K
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP; set-top box form factor replaces Chromecast line
products.provenance: Android Police review confirmed: MediaTek MT8696 chipset (Google declined to confirm officially but MT8696 identified by reviewers), 4 GB RAM, 32 GB storage (23 GB usable), 4K/60fps, Dolby Vision/HDR10/HDR10+/HLG, WiFi 5 (2.4/5 GHz, no WiFi 6 or 6E), Gigabit Ethernet (built-in), included voice remote, price $99. 9to5Google review corroborated WiFi 5 and Ethernet. Wikipedia Chromecast article confirmed: announced August 6 2024, 32 GB storage, 4 GB RAM, Ethernet port, $99. Note: Android Police reported WiFi 5 returning over WiFi 6; $99 confirmed.

products.priceNote: US launch MSRP; 1080p max output, HDMI dongle
